# Temple Scroll Column 50 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 50 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**50:1** If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons —

**50:2** and the firstborn son belongs to the unloved wife —

**50:3** then on the day he apportions his estate to his sons, he may not designate the son of the beloved wife as firstborn in preference to the son of the unloved wife, who is the actual firstborn.

**50:4** He shall acknowledge the firstborn status of the unloved wife's son by granting him a double portion of all his possessions, for he is the first issue of his vigor, and the right of primogeniture belongs to him.

**50:5** If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons — he shall not transfer the birthright.

**50:6** The firstborn is the son of the unloved wife — he may not treat the beloved wife's son as firstborn in place of the unloved wife's son who is the true firstborn.

**50:7** For the right of primogeniture belongs to the unloved wife's son; he is the first issue of his vigor.

**50:8** If a man has a defiant and rebellious son who refuses to obey his father's voice or his mother's voice —

**50:9** and they have disciplined him, yet he refuses to heed them —

**50:10** his father and mother shall seize him and bring him before the elders of his city, at the gate of his locality.

**50:11** If a man has a defiant and rebellious son who refuses to obey his father's voice or his mother's voice, and they have disciplined him, yet he refuses to heed them —

**50:12** his father and mother shall declare to the elders of his city: This son of ours is defiant and rebellious; he refuses to obey us; he is a profligate and a drunkard.

**50:13** All the men of his city shall stone him to death; thus you shall purge the evil from your midst, and all Israel shall hear and take warning.

**50:14** If a man has committed a capital offense and is executed, and you impale him on a stake —

**50:15** his corpse shall not remain on the stake overnight. You shall bury him that same day, for an impaled body is an affront to God; you shall not defile the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.

**50:16** You shall not observe your brother's ox or sheep straying and disregard them; you shall without fail return them to your brother.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 50 presents Deuteronomy 21:15-23 and begins 22:1. LOGOS renders senuah as "unloved" rather than "hated" — the Hebrew comparative idiom expresses relative preference. "Primogeniture" for bekhorah captures the legal concept. The rebellious son law (vv. 8-13) represents communal discipline for severe filial disobedience. The hanging provision (vv. 14-15) uses "impale on a stake" following recent scholarship on talah al etz. "Affront to God" for qilelat elohim avoids the ambiguity of "curse of God."*
